content.text:
{
  "version": "1.0",
  "assets": [
    {
      "name": "stg_orders",
      "type": "model",
      "description": "One row per source order, including all lifecycle statuses.",
      "owner": "data-platform",
      "lifecycle": "active",
      "grain": ["order_id"],
      "canonical": true
    },
    {
      "name": "customer_orders",
      "type": "model",
      "description": "Completed-order metrics at one row per customer; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.",
      "owner": "analytics",
      "lifecycle": "active",
      "grain": ["customer_id"],
      "canonical": true
    },
    {
      "name": "daily_revenue",
      "type": "model",
      "description": "Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.",
      "owner": "finance-analytics",
      "lifecycle": "active",
      "grain": ["order_date"],
      "canonical": true
    }
  ]
}

select
    order_date,
    count(*) as completed_order_count,
    sum(amount) as completed_revenue
from {{ ref('stg_orders') }}
where status = 'completed'
group by order_date

version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_orders
    description: One row per source order, including all lifecycle statuses.
    config:
      meta:
        owner: data-platform
        lifecycle: active
        grain: order_id
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        description: Source order identifier.
        data_tests: [not_null, unique]
      - name: customer_id
        description: Customer that placed the order.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: status
        description: Current order lifecycle status.
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [completed, refunded, cancelled]
      - name: order_date
        description: Date the order was placed.
        data_tests: [not_null]

  - name: customer_orders
    description: Completed-order metrics at one row per customer; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.
    config:
      meta:
        owner: analytics
        lifecycle: active
        grain: customer_id
    columns:
      - name: customer_id
        description: Customer identifier and model grain.
        data_tests: [not_null, unique]
      - name: completed_order_count
        description: Number of completed orders for the customer.

  - name: daily_revenue
    description: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.
    config:
      meta:
        owner: finance-analytics
        lifecycle: active
        grain: order_date
    columns:
      - name: order_date
        description: Order date and model grain.
        data_tests: [not_null, unique]
      - name: completed_order_count
        description: Number of completed orders on the date.
      - name: completed_revenue
        description: Sum of completed order amounts on the date.

select
    cast(order_id as integer) as order_id,
    cast(customer_id as integer) as customer_id,
    cast(status as varchar) as status,
    cast(order_date as date) as order_date,
    cast(amount as decimal(12, 2)) as amount
from {{ ref('raw_orders') }}

content.sql: SELECT order_date, completed_order_count, completed_revenue FROM daily_revenue ORDER BY order_date

action.rationale: Align the effective catalog description with the model's completed-only filter and the model metadata description.
action.value: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.

verification.equals: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.

findings.claim: The catalog override says revenue is from all orders, but the SQL includes only rows where status = 'completed'. The catalog description should state that refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.

plan.summary: Found one catalog metadata drift for daily_revenue: its override describes revenue from all orders, while the model filters to completed orders only.
